'''Alexander Klibanov''' is the Novartis Professor of Biological Engineering and Chemistry at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]<ref name="MITBE">{{cite journal |title=Alexander M. Klibanov, PhD |url=https://be.mit.edu/directory/alexander-m-klibanov |journal=Applied Biochemistry and Biotechnology |year=2014 |publisher=MIT |doi=10.1007/s12010-013-0593-4 |pmid=24158590 |accessdate=15 November 2020|last1=Liu |first1=H. |last2=Kim |first2=Y. |last3=Mello |first3=K. |last4=Lovaasen |first4=J. |last5=Shah |first5=A. |last6=Rice |first6=N. |last7=Yim |first7=J. H. |last8=Pappas |first8=D. |last9=Klibanov |first9=A. M. |volume=172 |issue=3 |pages=1254–1264 |hdl=1721.1/107156 |s2cid=207355690 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> and a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]]. He was also elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] (1993) for research in enzyme and protein technology and contributions to the field of biocatalysis in nonaqueous solvents.

He is most notable for greatly advancing the field of non-[[aqueous]] enzymology, that is, developing methods to allow [[enzyme]]s to function in media such as [[organic solvent]]s, rather than water.

Klibanov earned a Master of Science in chemistry and a PhD in chemical enzymology from Moscow University in Russia. He joined MIT as assistant professor of applied biochemistry in 1979 after two years at the [[University of California, San Diego]] where he did postdoctoral research.<ref name="MITBE" />
